response: Octogenarians are not necessarily at high risk for carotid endarterectomy. According to the available data, combined end points for adverse events are acceptable in the octogenarian, and age alone should not place patients in the high-risk category for carotid endarterectomy. In fact, carotid endarterectomy remains the gold standard for treatment of extracranial carotid disease in all age groups, including octogenarians. This suggests that with proper evaluation and management, octogenarians can undergo carotid endarterectomy with acceptable risks.
